section.content: 本发明提供了可利霉素生物合成基因簇，含有的基因至少包括聚酮合酶基因5个(orf10‑14)，与糖基合成相关的orf有16个(9、16‑22、24、26、28、29、33‑35、41)，与糖基转移相关的6个orf(7、8、30‑32、40)中的至少5个，此外，还含有外源引入的碳霉糖4”‑O‑异戊酰转移酶基因orf44。通过基因簇序列信息和结构分析，可以进一步对其产生菌进行遗传操作，获得新型、更有效的抗生素，如通过基因操作来改变其PKS合成模块式结构、进行内酯环后修饰的改变、糖基因的置换或修饰，创造新的大环内酯类抗生素，也可以通过对抗性基因或调节基因的遗传操作，提高抗生素的产量。所提供的基因及其蛋白质、抗体，也可用以筛选和发展可用于医药、工业、农业的化合物或蛋白。

The invention provides a colimycin biosynthesis gene cluster, which contains at least 5 genes (orf10-14) of polyketide synthase, 16 orfs (9, 16-22, 24, 26, 28, 29, 33-35 and 41) related to glycosyl synthesis, at least 5 of 6 orfs (7, 8, 30-32 and 40) related to glycosyl transfer, and also contains exogenously introduced mycaminose 4' -O-isovaleryltransferase gene orf 44. Through gene cluster sequence information and structural analysis, genetic manipulation can be further carried out on the producing strain to obtain novel and more effective antibiotics, for example, the PKS synthetic modular structure is changed through genetic manipulation, the change of lactone ring post-modification and the replacement or modification of sugar genes are carried out, new macrolide antibiotics are created, and the yield of the antibiotics can also be improved through the genetic manipulation on resistance genes or regulatory genes. The provided gene, protein and antibody thereof can also be used for screening and developing compounds or proteins which can be used for medicine, industry and agriculture.

Colimycin biosynthesis gene clusterThe present application is a divisional application of chinese patent application 201511028754.9.

The original application date: 2015.12.31

Original application number: 201511028754.9

The invention of the original application is named: colimycin biosynthesis gene cluster

The technical field is as follows:

the invention belongs to the field of microbial gene resources and genetic engineering, and particularly relates to cloning, analysis, functional research and application of a genetic engineering antibiotic biosynthesis gene cluster.

Technical background:

the colimycin is named shengmycin and bitspiramycin, and is a 16-membered ring macrolide antibiotic developed by utilizing synthetic biology technology [ patent number: ZL971044406, ZL 021487715], is spiramycin which takes 4 '-O-isovaleryl spiramycin III, II and I as main components and is multiply acylated at 4' -hydroxyl, wherein the III component accounts for more than 30 percent, the II component accounts for about 25 percent, and the I component does not exceed 10 percent.

Structural formula of colimycin

Isovalerylspiramycin III: r is COCH2CH3 R′＝COCH2CH(CH3)2

Isovaleryl spiramycin ii: r is COCH3 R′＝COCH2CH(CH3)2

Isovaleryl spiramycin i: r H R ═ COCH2CH(CH3)2

The kelimycin has strong activity on gram-positive bacteria, and has antibacterial activity on erythromycin and beta-lactam antibiotic resistant bacteria, bacillus influenzae, gonococcus, legionella, bacteroides fragilis and clostridium perfringens. Especially has stronger activity to mycoplasma pneumoniae, chlamydia trachomatis and chlamydia pneumoniae [ Yulan Xiang, etc., Sichuan journal of physiological science; 1998,20(3), patent No.: 2003101224209], has better antibiotic post-effect and antibiotic sub-inhibitory concentration effect. It has no complete cross-resistance with the same class of drugs. Pharmacokinetic studies show that the kelimycin has higher lipophilicity, strong intracellular antibacterial activity, fast oral absorption, high absolute bioavailability, strong tissue permeability, higher tissue concentration than plasma concentration, wide tissue distribution, long elimination half-life, and long in vivo maintenance time [ sunlivin et al, chinese pharmacological bulletin 2000, 16 (6): 694-8; magnifications, et al, J chromatography b.2003, 791: 45, a first step of; schedule et al, Asian Journal of Drug Metabolism and Pharmacokinetics.2003, 3 (2): 134; schwann et al, Chinese Chemical letter 2004,15: 431; schwarken et al, Acta Pharmacological Sinica,2004,25:1396 ]. Pharmacological, toxicological and completed clinical three-phase research results show that the treatment effect of the kelimycin for treating respiratory tract infection is definite, the adverse reaction rate is low, particularly the damage to the liver is small, and the safety is good [ Linnahong Tian et al, eighth national antibiotic academic conference paper compilation 1997, p.167; zhao Chun Yan et al, China antibiotic journal 1998,23 (4): 306; sunset et al, journal of chinese antibiotics 2001, 26 (1): 49-51]. The kelimycin is a direct product of fermentation of genetically engineered bacteria obtained by using a gene recombination technology, has simple and convenient preparation process, can effectively avoid chemical pollution and save energy. The oral preparation is convenient to take, only needs to be taken once every day, is beneficial to improving the medication compliance of patients, and is also convenient to enter a basic medical insurance medicine series.

The colimycin is a fermentation product of a genetic engineering bacterium (Streptomyces spiromyces WSJ-1) obtained by cloning and expressing a gene of a carbomycin producing bacterium 4' -O-isovaleryltransferase in a spiramycin producing bacterium (Streptomyces spiromyces F21) by utilizing a gene recombination technology. The spiramycin-producing strain (Streptomyces spiramycin F21) was isolated in 1982 from soil in chang county, gansu, and the strain has morphological culture characteristics, physiological and biochemical characteristics, cell wall chemical composition, 16S rRNA gene sequence and 5 housekeeping gene protein levels in phylogenetic tree analysis, and has no commonalities with Streptomyces ambofaciens 23877 and reported Streptomyces ATCC reported abroad, so that the spiramycin-producing strain is most likely to be a new Streptomyces strain [ sarong et al, microbiological report 2012, 39 (4): 503-514].

Sequencing of the gene cluster involved in spiramycin biosynthesis in the spiramycin-producing strain Streptomyces ambofaciens ATCC23877 [ Karray F. Microbiology 2007,153:4111-4122], other macrolide antibiotics such as avermectin, canavalidamycin, erythromycin, chalcone, tylosin and midecamycin biosynthetic gene cluster sequences have also been reported [ Ikeda H. et al Nat. Biotechnology.2003, 21(5):526-531, Haydock et al Microbiology 2005,151, 3161-3169; oliynyk M.et al Nat.Biotechnol.2007,25(4): 447-453; (vi) Wards L.et al Antichronob.Agents & Chemotherapy 2004,48(12): 4703-4712; cundiffe E.et al Antonie Van Leeuwenhoek 2001,79(3-4): 229-234; midoh Naoki et al US patent 7070980 ]. The total length of the macrolide antibiotic biosynthesis gene cluster is about 50-80kb, and the common characteristics of the macrolide antibiotic biosynthesis gene cluster are that the macrolide antibiotic biosynthesis gene cluster consists of polyketone synthase (PKS) which codes a 16-membered macrolide ring biosynthesis modular structure, polyketone synthesis elongation unit related enzyme, enzyme which is responsible for modification of different groups of a lactone ring, genes of glycosyl synthesis and transfer related enzyme, genes related to resistance and regulation functions and the like. Macrolides are catalyzed by PKS, which consists of modular structural forms, to form a number of simple carboxylic acid molecules by successive condensation reactions in a manner similar to fatty acid biosynthesis. Each module is responsible for only one condensation reaction during polyketide chain formation and comprises AT least a β -ketoester acyl synthase (KS) domain, an Acyltransferase (AT) domain, and an Acyl Carrier Protein (ACP) domain. In addition, it may comprise a β -Ketoacyl Reductase (KR) domain, a Dehydratase (DH) domain and an acyl reductase (ER) domain, which determine the reduction step in which the extension unit is added. At the same time, the role of Thioesterase (TE) domain is also required to catalyze the cyclization and release of the polyketide chain. Finally, the structure of various macrolide antibiotics can be formed through modification steps such as hydroxylation, methylation, methoxylation, acylation and the like. Typically, macrolides are linked to different numbers of sugar (or sugar amine) groups, e.g., the three sugar groups of kelimycin, which are forosamine, mycaminose, and mycaminose, respectively. They are responsible for the synthesis of glycosyl groups and for the transfer of enzymes involved. Resistance genes confer the ability of the producer to antagonize the production of antibiotics by itself, and are commonly associated with ABC transporters. The gene related to the regulation function is involved in the regulation and control of self-biosynthesis antibiotics.

Through gene cluster sequence information and structural analysis, genetic operation can be further carried out on the producing strain to obtain a novel and more effective antibiotic, for example, a novel macrolide antibiotic is created by changing a PKS synthetic modular structure, carrying out the change of lactone ring post-modification, and replacing or modifying a sugar gene through genetic operation; the yield of antibiotics can also be increased by genetic manipulation of resistance genes or regulatory genes. (1) polyketide synthase gene orf10-14, 5 genes in total;

(2) 9 genes of orf1, orf4-6, 15 and 36-39 related to polyketide synthesis elongation unit and modification;

(3) 16 genes of orf9, 16-22, 24, 26, 28, 29, 33-35 and 41 related to glycosyl synthesis;

(4) 6 genes of gene orf7, 8, 30-32 and 40 related to glycosyl transfer;

(5) 2 genes in total with resistance-associated genes orf3 and 25;

(6) 4 genes in total and biosynthesis regulation related genes orf2, 23, 27 and 42;

(7) the genetic engineering bacteria marker gene orf43 (thiostrepton-thiostrepton, tsr resistance gene) introduced by exogenous and the mycaminose 4' -O-isovaleryltransferase gene orf44 linked with the gene are 2 genes in total.

And colimycin resistance related genes orf3 and 25, which are 2 genes in total, wherein: orf3 encodes 23S rRNA methylase; orf25 encodes ABC transporters that confer resistance to self-producing antibiotics by methylation of ribosomal RNA and by pumping mechanisms.

4 genes related to the biosynthesis and regulation of the colimycin, orf2, 23, 27 and 42, wherein: orf2 encodes a TetR family transcriptional regulation inhibitor, possibly involved in negative regulation of the biosynthesis of colimycin; orf23, 42 encode two positive regulatory transcription factors, respectively, the latter is a pathway specific positive regulatory factor, directly regulates the biosynthesis of the colimycin; orf27 encodes a gtpase that may regulate the biosynthesis of colimycin by regulating cellular functions.

Related to the biosynthesis of the colimycin, orf43 and orf44 are exogenously introduced, wherein orf43 codes for a 23S rRNA methylase gene related to the resistance of thiostrepton, the gene is linked with a mycaminose 4' -O-isovaleryltransferase gene orf44, and the resistance expression of the gene can provide a differential marker for the colimycin gene engineering bacteria.

The complementary sequences of seq.1 and 2 of the invention can be obtained at any time according to the DNA base complementary principle. The nucleotide sequence or partial nucleotide sequence of seq.1, 2 can be obtained by Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) or by digesting the corresponding DNA with a suitable restriction enzyme or using other suitable techniques. The nucleotide sequence or partial nucleotide sequence provided by the invention can be used for obtaining a gene similar to the biosynthesis gene of the colimycin from other organisms by using a Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) method or a Southern hybridization method by using DNA containing the sequence of the invention as a probe.

The invention also provides a way for constructing a recombinant DNA vector by at least obtaining partial DNA sequences in the seq.1 and 2.

The invention also provides a method for blocking the biosynthesis gene of the rokitamycin, wherein at least one gene comprises the nucleotide sequence in the seq.1.

The nucleotide sequence or at least partial sequence cloned gene or DNA fragment provided by the invention can obtain a novel colimycin derivative by blocking one or more steps of the biosynthesis of the colimycin. Comprising a DNA fragment or gene, can be used to increase the yield of the colimycin or its derivatives.

The cloned DNA of the nucleotide sequence or at least partial sequence provided by the present invention can be used to locate more library plasmids from a genomic library. These library plasmids contain at least a partial sequence of the present invention and also DNA of the region adjacent to the genome of the gene of the bacteria producing the calicheamicin.

The nucleotide sequences provided by the present invention may be modified or mutated. Routes include insertion or displacement, polymerase chain reaction, error-mediated polymerase chain reaction, site-specific mutagenesis, reconnection of different sequences or mutagenesis by ultraviolet light or chemical reagents.

The nucleotide sequence provided by the invention can be directly evolved through different parts of the sequence or homologous sequences from other sources (DNA shuffling).

Fragments or domains or modules or genes of the nucleotide sequences or at least part of the sequences of the invention may be used to construct polyketide synthase libraries or polyketide synthase derivative libraries or combinatorial libraries. Novel polyketides are produced by deleting or inactivating one or more polyketide synthase domains, modules or genes from the same or different polyketide synthase systems, or adding one or more polyketide synthase domains, modules or genes.

The nucleotide sequences of the biosynthetic modifying genes, glycosyl syntheses and glycosyltransferase genes of the invention provide a way to obtain the calicheamicin derivatives by deleting, replacing or modifying these glycosyl syntheses, transfers and modifying genes.

The nucleotide sequence or at least partial sequence fragment or structural domain or module or gene provided by the invention can improve the yield of the colimycin or the derivative thereof by adding times.

The nucleotide sequence or at least a part of the sequence of the cloned gene of the invention can be expressed in an exogenous host by a suitable expression system to obtain a modified or higher biological activity or higher yield of the colimycin. Such exogenous hosts include Streptomyces, Escherichia coli, Bacillus, yeast, plants, and animals, among others.

The nucleotide sequences of the invention, or at least part of the sequence of the gene or gene cluster, can be expressed in heterologous hosts and their function in the metabolic chain of the host is known by DNA chip technology.

The amino acid sequences of the invention, or at least part of the sequences of the polypeptides, may have biological activity, even new biological activity, after removal or substitution of one or more amino acids, or may have improved yields or optimized protein kinetics or other properties sought to be achieved. By deletion of appropriate techniques, linking the amino acid sequences of the invention, new proteins or enzymes can be obtained, which in turn produce new or related products.

The amino acid sequence provided by the invention can be used for separating a needed protein and can be used for preparing an antibody.

The amino acid sequence provided by the invention provides possibility for predicting the three-dimensional structure of polyketide synthase.

The gene, protein and antibody provided by the invention can also be used for screening and developing compounds or proteins for medicine, industry and agriculture.

EXAMPLE 2 verification of the function of the seq.1 Gene information by Gene disruption

Genes IA-W1 and IA-W42, IA-W4, 17, 21, 23 and 27 and the like at two ends of a gene cluster are selected for blocking to obtain mutant strains, and experiments prove that the capacity of the blocked strains for producing the rokitamycin is changed or the rokitamycin is not produced any more. Thus, it was suggested that the obtained gene cluster information is necessary for the production of the rokitamycin. Designing a primer according to the coding gene and the upstream and downstream sequences thereof, and inserting a proper enzyme cutting site, wherein the sequences of the primer are shown in Table 2.

TABLE 2 primer sequences designed for Gene Block experiments

Obtaining corresponding homologous Gene fragments through PCR amplification respectively, adopting corresponding enzyme cutting sites, and inserting a screening marker resistance Gene (apramycin-Am) to connect to a temperature-sensitive vector pKC1139[ Bierman M.et al Gene 1992; 116(1):43-9] or Escherichia coli/Streptomyces vector pGH112 (Youbao Bio Inc.), to obtain recombinant plasmids containing homologous genes, transforming the recombinant plasmids into a kelimycin-producing strain through protoplast transformation, and performing single colony separation after culturing to obtain homologous fragment double-crossover gene-disrupted strains. IA-W43-O-acyltransferase gene blocking recombinant plasmid construction and gene homologous fragment double exchange are schematically shown in FIG. 3. The schematic construction of IA-W42 transcription regulatory gene blocking recombinant plasmid is shown in FIG. 4.

PCR verification of total DNA of the blocking strain and the original strain was performed using the corresponding primers, respectively, as shown in FIGS. 5A and B. The result of FIG. 5A shows that 613bp of gene orf4 encoding the IA-W4 gene disruption mutant is deleted. The results of PCR verification are shown in FIG. 5B as an example, indicating that the length of PCR product shows an increase in comparison with the original strain due to the insertion of the selection marker resistance gene into the gene encoding the mutation-blocking mutant.

Fermentation experiments and HPLC detection of products prove that IA-W4 blocks the mutant strain to not produce 4 '-isovaleryl spiramycin III and II any more, but uses 4' -isovaleryl spiramycin I as a main component (figure 6). The IA-W43-O-acyltransferase gene in the seq.1 gene information provided by the invention is proved to participate in the biosynthesis of the rokitamycin, and the interruption of the gene leads the mutant strain to lose the function of acylating the hydroxyl at the 3-position of the rokitamycin lactone ring.

Fermentation experiments and product antibacterial activity and HPLC detection of other gene-blocking strains prove that the blocking strains can not generate active rokitamycin any more. The seq.1 gene cluster provided by the present invention is involved in the biosynthesis of rokitamycin.

EXAMPLE 3 Gene transfer into a Strain producing Colimycin and selection of a disrupted Strain

3.1 preparation of protoplasts: inoculating fresh kelimycin producing bacteria slant spore to R2YE liquid culture medium, shaking and culturing at 28 deg.C and 220rpm for 48 hr, transferring the culture medium into fresh R supplemented with 0.5% glycine at 10% transferring amount2YE liquid culture medium, 28 ℃ shaking culture for 20 h. Taking 10ml of bacterial liquid in a centrifuge tube, centrifuging at 3000rpm to collect mycelium, and using P-buffer for precipitation

Washing for 2 times, suspending with appropriate amount of P-buffer, adding lysozyme P-buffer solution (final concentration of 2mg/ml), mixing, keeping temperature in 37 deg.C water bath for 30-45min, and shaking once every 10-15 min. The formation of protoplasts was observed under a phase contrast microscope (10X 40), and when microscopic examination revealed that most of the hyphae had formed protoplasts, the enzymatic hydrolysis was stopped. The mixture was filtered through absorbent cotton, and the filtrate was centrifuged and washed 2 times with P-buffer. Finally, 1ml of P-buffer is used for suspending the protoplast, and the protoplast is subpackaged into an EP tube and a 100 mu l tube for standby at the temperature of 70 ℃ below zero.

3.2 transformation of protoplasts with plasmid DNA: adding 10 μ l plasmid DNA solution into 100 μ l protoplast, flicking the tube wall, mixing, rapidly adding 400 μ l P-buffer containing 25% PEG-1000 (product of Koch-light of UK), blowing, sucking, mixing, standing at room temperature for 5min, spreading 200 μ l protoplast on dehydrated R2YE plates were incubated at 28 ℃ for 20 hours, covered with 50. mu.g/ml tsr of sterile water, incubated at 28 ℃ for 5 to 7 days, and transformants were picked.

3.3 screening of Gene-disrupted mutant

The transformants were picked up in a medium supplemented with Tsr 50. mu.g/ml

Preparing deionized water, naturally adjusting pH value, sterilizing at 15 pounds, and sterilizing at 121 ℃ for 30 min.

Culturing at 28 ℃ for 5-7 days, carrying out four-five generations in a culture medium without adding drugs, separating monospores, correspondingly screening the monospores on a culture medium with adriamycin (Am 50 mu g/ml), and screening out gene-blocked strains which grow on Am and do not grow on Tsr. And (3) selecting a blocking strain with stable resistance marker expression, extracting genome DNA, performing PCR amplification by using corresponding primers in example 2, and judging the correctness of gene blocking according to the size of a product and DNA sequencing.

EXAMPLE 4 fermentation of a Strain producing colimycin and a Gene-disrupted Strain, detection and identification of the Activity of the product

4.1 fermentation

Strain in slant medium (g/L):

preparing deionized water, naturally adjusting pH value, sterilizing at 15 pounds, and sterilizing at 121 ℃ for 30 min.

Culturing at 28 deg.C for 10-12d, digging and inoculating to 100mL triangular flask containing 30mL fermentation medium, and shake culturing at 28 deg.C for 96-120 h.

Fermentation medium (g/L):

deionized water preparation, 15 pounds of sterilization, 121 ℃, 30 min.

4.2 fermentation product activity detection:

after the fermentation liquor is centrifuged and supernatant fluid is diluted, bacillus subtilis is taken as a detection bacterium, and the reference is made to a microbiological detection method of acetylspiramycin in 2005 edition (second edition) of pharmacopoeia of the people's republic of China. The measurements were carried out by cup and dish method, using standard curve method.

4.3 extraction and identification of fermentation products:

centrifuging the fermentation liquid at room temperature of 3000rpm for 15min, adjusting the pH of the supernatant to 8.5 with 1M NaOH, extracting with 1/2 volume of ethyl acetate, taking out the ethyl acetate phase, drying in a dish, volatilizing, dissolving in chromatographic pure methanol, filtering, and injecting 10-20 μ l. And (3) chromatography: shimadzu LC-10ATvp liquid chromatograph, diode array detector, chromatographic column: kromasil C18(4.5 mm. times.150 mm, 5 μm), mobile phase: CH (CH)3OH/1％NaH2PO4(55:45), detection wavelength: 231nm, flow rate: column temperature 1 ml/min: at 25 ℃. A4' -isovaleryl spiramycin I biosynthesis gene cluster is characterized in that the biosynthesis gene cluster has 43 genes in total, and specifically comprises the following genes:</claim-text>(1) polyketide synthase gene orf10-14, 5 genes in total;</claim-text>(2) genes orf1, orf5-6, 15 and 36-39 related to polyketide synthesis elongation units and modification, wherein the total number of the genes is 8;</claim-text>(3) 16 genes of orf9, 16-22, 24, 26, 28, 29, 33-35 and 41 related to glycosyl synthesis;</claim-text>(4) 6 genes of gene orf7, 8, 30-32 and 40 related to glycosyl transfer;</claim-text>(5) 2 genes in total with resistance-associated genes orf3 and 25;</claim-text>(6) 4 genes in total and biosynthesis regulation related genes orf2, 23, 27 and 42;</claim-text>(7) the genetic engineering bacteria marker gene orf43 introduced by exogenous and the mycaminose 4' -O-isovaleryl transferase gene orf44 linked with the gene orf43 totally have 2 genes;</claim-text>wherein the nucleotide sequence of each gene is respectively selected from orf1(1-645), orf2(1810-1208), orf3(3133-2285), orf5(4846-5511), orf6(7150-5801), orf7(8444-7179), orf8(9729-8482), orf9(10543-9830), orf10(16215-10543), orf11(21076-16328), orf12(32511-21124), orf13(38599-32585), orf14(52259-38643), orf15(53099-54310), orf16(54495-54845), orf17(54842-56041), orf18 (365638-56946), orf 5758 (930-36575639), orf 575639 (369636967), orf 6172 (36725772-36725774), orf 6057725774 (367272-367272), 36725774), 3672725774 (36727272), 367272725774), 36727272725774 (367272), 367272725774 (369872), 369868-369868), 367272 (367272), 36725774), 367272 (36725774), 367272), 36727272727272), 36725768 (367272), 36725768, 367272), 369868 (367272), 20, orf29(74601-73561), orf30(74913-76160), orf31(76218-77486), orf32(77606-78781), orf33(78783-79775), orf34(79772-80779), orf35(82055-80823), orf36(83164-82052), orf37(84400-83279), orf38(84713-84393), orf39(85576-84710), orf40(85825-87042), orf41(87094-87702), orf42(89315-88143), and orf43(866-60) and orf44(2337-1174) in seq.2 of a foreign gene not linked with seq1.</claim-text></claim-text>2. A biosynthetic gene cluster according to claim 1, characterized in that said 5 polyketide synthase genes encode a polyketide body biosynthetic enzyme catalyzing the synthesis of the 16-membered lactone ring of colimycin, the nucleotide sequence or the complementary sequence of said 5 polyketide synthase genes orf10-14 corresponding to the amino acid sequence IA-W10 as shown in seq.12, IA-W11 as shown in seq.13, IA-W12 as shown in seq.14, IA-W13 as shown in seq.15 and IA-W14 as shown in seq.16.</claim-text></claim-text>3. The biosynthetic gene cluster of claim 1 or 2, wherein 5 polyketide synthases comprise a module or domain comprising an amino acid sequence corresponding to the nucleotide sequence or complement of a Ketosynthase (KS), an Acyltransferase (AT), a Ketoreductase (KR), a Dehydratase (DH), an Enoyl Reductase (ER), an Acyl Carrier Protein (ACP), a thioesterase domain.</claim-text></claim-text>4. A biosynthetic gene cluster according to claim 1, characterized in that the nucleotide sequence or the complementary sequence of the genes orf9, 16-22, 24, 26, 28, 29, 33-35, 41 relevant for the sugar synthesis is represented by the amino acid sequence IA-W9 as shown in seq.11, IA-W16 as shown in seq.18, IA-W17 as shown in seq.19, IA-W18 as shown in seq.20, IA-W19 as shown in seq.21, IA-W20 as shown in seq.22, IA-W21 as shown in seq.23, IA-W22 as shown in seq.24, IA-W24 as shown in seq.26, IA-W26 as shown in seq.28, IA-W28 as shown in seq.30, IA-W29 as shown in seq.31, IA-W33 as shown in seq.35, IA-W34 as shown in seq.36, IA-W3985 as shown in seq.38.</claim-text></claim-text>5. The biosynthetic gene cluster of claim 1 or 4, wherein in the genes involved in glycosyl synthesis, orf18,19 and 28 encode enzymes involved in synthesis, dehydration and isomerization of the basic glycosyl unit of calicheamicin; orf9, 20, 21, 24, 26 and 29 encode enzymes involved in the N-dimethylation, 2,3 dehydration, amination, isomerization, dehydration and ketoreductase of NDP-hexosamine synthesis; orf16, 17, 22 encodes enzymes involved in the isomerization, amination and N-demethylation of mycaminosamine NDP-aminohexoses; orf33, 34, 35 and 41 encode enzymes for the reduction, methylation and isomerization of mycaminose NDP-aminohexonyl.</claim-text></claim-text>6. The biosynthetic gene cluster of claim 1, wherein the nucleotide sequence or the complementary sequence of the gene orf7, 8, 30-32, 40 associated with glycosyl transfer is represented by IA-W7 as seq.9, IA-W8 as seq.10, IA-W30 as seq.32, IA-W31 as seq.33, IA-W32 as seq.34 and IA-W40 as seq.42.</claim-text></claim-text>7. The biosynthetic gene cluster of claim 1 or 6, wherein the glycosyltransfer related gene: orf7 encodes a myceliophthora glycosaminoglycans glycosylase; orf8 encodes its glycosylated accessory protein; orf31 and 32 encode forosamine glycosylase; orf30 encodes its glycosylated accessory protein; orf40 encodes a mycaminose glycosylase.</claim-text></claim-text>8. The biosynthetic gene cluster of claim 1, wherein the nucleotide sequence or the complementary sequence of the exogenously introduced mycaminose 4 "-O-isovaleryltransferase gene orf44 corresponds to an amino acid sequence IA-W44 as shown in seq.46.</claim-text>
